rules.title: Massachusetts limit on upfront charges by lessors (G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a landlord may only require first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit, and a lock-change fee. Application, screening, pet, cleaning and amenity fees charged by the landlord are not allowed; only licensed brokers may charge fees, under 254 C.M.R. 7.
rules.quoted_span: prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks (MGL Ch 186 Section 15B).
rules.key_value: Only first, last, security deposit, and lock fee; no landlord application fee
rules.effective_date_note: Document says the law has been in effect since the 1970s; no precise date given.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source; licensed brokers may charge fees under 254 C.M.R. 7 and landlord-brokers are uncertain.

rules.title: Massachusetts licensed broker fee disclosure rules (254 C.M.R. 7)
rules.requirement: Licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees if they comply with board regulations. The broker must give written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting.
rules.quoted_span: the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.
rules.key_value: Written broker fee disclosure at first personal meeting
rules.conflict_note: The document does not mention the 2025 broker-fee rule (G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD½).

parsed.doc_summary: A Massachusetts landlord association article explains that G.L. c. 186, § 15B bars landlords from charging application fees, while licensed brokers may charge fees under 254 C.M.R. 7.
